newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's Q2 same-store sales negative.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's Q2 same-store sales negative.

text.p: McDonald's Corp said Thursday its U.S. same-store sales were slightly negative for the second quarter, but were slightly positive for the first six months of the year.
The fast-food giant, which posted second quarter earnings of $0.63 a share -- in line with estimates and up from $0.59 a year ago -- said it expects record results in all of 1997.
"We are confident in our growth strategies and expect 1997 to be another record-breaking year," Michael Quinlan, chairman, said in a statement.
McDonald's said U.S. operating income in the second quarter fell to $340.2 million from $346.0 million. Outside the U.S., operating income rose to $416.8 million from $377.3 million a year ago.
"Our international results strengthened in the second quarter," James Cantalupo, president-international, said in a statement.

Second quarter systemwide sales in the U.S. rose three percent to $4.42 billion from $4.28 billion. Outside the U.S., second quarter systemwide sales rose 11 percent to $4.05 billion from $3.65 billion.
If exchange rates had remained at 1996 levels, second quarter foreign sales would have increased 18 percent.

"We operate about twice the number of restaurants outside the U.S. as our next largest globally branded competitor," Cantalupo said. "We intend to build from this strong position to capture an even greater share of the under-penetrated, growing global market."
McDonald's has nearly 22,000 restaurants worldwide, including more than 12,000 in the United States.
McDonald's said it plans to open 2,400 new restaurants globally this year, with about 80 percent to be outside the United States.
Commenting on U.S. results, Jack Greenberg, chairman of the domestic unit, reiterated that McDonald's considers 1997 to be a "year of transition for our U.S. business."
"I remain very optimistic about our long-term opportunities to grow profitably in the domestic marketplace," Greenberg said in a statement.
Last week, McDonald's announced a new line-up of U.S. executives as part of its plan to decentralize its domestic operations.
